newsitem.title: UK: Britain mulls banning N.Ireland guerrilla groups.
newsitem.headline: Britain mulls banning N.Ireland guerrilla groups.

text.p: Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary said on Tuesday that she was considering outlawing two guerrilla groups responsible for violence over the past year.

Mo Mowlam told reporters she would make an announcement "in the next 24 to 48 hours" as to whether she would ban the pro-British Loyalist Volunteer Force (LVF) and pro-Irish Continuity Army Council (CAC).

Formal banning would make membership of either group a crime and add to the list of proscribed organisations in Northern Ireland whose war for and against British rule in the past 29 years has killed 3,200 people.
"I have to look at the information as to whether these organisations, the CAC and the LVF, should be proscribed and I am examining that case at the moment," she said.

Mowlam was speaking during a break in Belfast peace talks from which Sinn Fein, political wing of the main Irish Republican Army guerrilla group, is banned because of the IRA's failure to restore a broken truce.
The LVF split from Northern Ireland's mainstream Loyalist movement, which is officially maintaining a ceasefire in its campaign to maintain British rule of the province.
It claimed responsibility for an aborted bomb attack on the Irish border town of Dundalk last week, accusing the Dublin government of interfering in British affairs in Northern Ireland.
Loyalists trace their name to allegiance to the British crown. Three other Loyalist groups have been banned for years and jointly declared a ceasefire in October 1994.
The CAC is a shadowy republican splinter group which was thought responsible for an attempted car bomb in Belfast three weeks ago and an attack on a country hotel in July last year.
It shares the IRA's goals of ending British rule of Northern Ireland and reuniting it with the Republic of Ireland.
